 7:52 pm, October 24, 2026 No. 1 Miami cruises, No. 6 Indiana survives to start day
 Though No. 8 Texas Tech fell in an upset , the other ranked teams all picked up wins. Some easier than others.
 Playing as No. 1 for the first time since 2002, Miami (Fla.) routed Pitt 52-23 . Heisman hopefuls Darian Mensah (387 passing yards, 4 TDs) and Malachi Toney (16 catches, 194 yards, 3 touchdowns) dominated.
 No. 6 Indiana won at Michigan for the first time since 1967, getting by with a 13-6 OT win . The Wolverines out-gained IU 224 to 212, but Hoosiers QB Josh Hoover's 4-yard score in OT was the only TD on the day.
 A big first half carried No. 18 LSU to a 38-17 win against Auburn . LSU led 31-10 at the half with QB Sam Leavitt totaling four touchdowns and nearing 400 passing yards.
 A huge second half for No. 23 SMU meant a 59-20 win against Cal . The Mustangs outscored the Golden Bears 42-0 after halftime with QB Kevin Jennings breaking the program's career record for touchdowns. He had three TD passes on the day, giving him 74 in his career.
 Northwestern QB Aidan Chiles had five touchdowns (three passing, two rushing) for the No. 24 Wildcats in an easy 42-14 win against Rutgers .
 In non-top 25 land, FAU and Rice combined for 100 points in a 51-49 FAU win . Rice QB Gael Ochoa rushed for 259 yards and scored five total touchdowns and FAU QB Caden Veltkamp passed for 339 yards. FAU won despite allowing 608 yards.
 share with Facebook copy link 7:32 pm, October 24, 2026 UPSET: Cincinnati beats No. 8 Texas Tech
 And then there were four. Cincinnati has wiped out Texas Tech from the undefeated list . 
 Cincinnati rolled the No. 8 Red Raiders, winning 37-24  behind a big day from QB JC French IV and RB Cole Tabb. French recovered from a pick-six to finish with 172 passing yards, 46 rushing yards and four touchdowns. It's the Bearcats' first win against a top-10 team since beating No. 9 Notre Dame 24-13 on Oct. 2, 2021. It's the program's first top-10 win at home since defeating No. 7 Rutgers 30-11 on Nov. 18, 2006.
 Tabb picked up 173 yards and iced the game with a 58-yard run in the fourth quarter — the first rushing touchdown allowed by Texas Tech all season.
 share with Facebook copy link 6:48 pm, October 24, 2026 Rice QB up to 260 RUSHING yards
 The option offense is clicking for Rice — and the Owls have needed every yard against FAU.
 QB Gael Ochoa made his first career start for Rice and has found plenty of space, as he's rushed for 260 yards and four touchdowns on only eight attempts.
 That's 32.5 yards per attempt.
 you'll never believe it.....OCHOA TO THE HOUSE FOR THE 4TH TIME TODAY🤯 📺 | @ESPNCFB #BuiltToRise x @RiceFootball https://t.co/efWkdHrrvq
— The American (@American_Conf) October 24, 2026 
 As a team, Rice has 448 rushing yards, but FAU leads 44-42 through three quarters. FAU QB Caden Veltkamp has 331 passing yards and three touchdowns. 
 share with Facebook copy link 5:46 pm, October 24, 2026 Checking in as early games hit halftime
 We'll see if today's games end up anywhere close to as wild and upset-heavy as last week, but at least one top-10 team is already on major upset alert.
 Cincinnati is rolling at home against undefeated No. 8 Texas Tech , leading 24-6 at the half . QB JC French IV has three touchdown passes, while Red Raiders QB Will Hammond has struggled (82 yards, 1 INT).
 New No. 1 Miami has had a much easier time. The Hurricanes are up 31-7 at the half against Pitt thanks to Malachi Toney's 12 catches for 159 yards and two touchdowns. Darian Mensah has 274 yards and three touchdowns on 22 of 26 passing. Also in the ACC, No. 23 SMU is trailing Cal   20-17 .
 Over in the Big Ten, No. 6 Indiana has relied on its defense to take a 6-0 halftime lead at Michigan . Josh Hoover has only 60 passing yards for the Hoosiers, whose 22-game win streak ended last week against Ohio State. The Hoosiers' defense allowed only 93 yards in the first half to the Wolverines. Also in the league, No. 24 Northwestern is making it look easy against Rutgers , up 28-6 . The Wildcats posted 311 yards before the break, averaging 8.7 yards per carry.
 In the SEC, Sam Leavitt's strong first half has No. 18 LSU up 31-10 on Auburn . Leavitt has four total touchdowns, with WR Jackson Haris his favorite target (139 yards, 2 TD catches).
 share with Facebook copy link 5:34 pm, October 24, 2026 Miami star Toney with another huge game
 Miami WR Malachi Toney is at it again.
 One week after his 11 catches, 154 yards and two scores helped the Hurricanes escape rival Florida State, the star is dominating against Pitt.
 In the program's first game as the nation's top team since 2002, Miami has had little trouble against the Panthers, leading 31-7 . Toney is a major reason why, posting 12 catches for 159 yards and two touchdowns — his second going for 53 yards as he eluded tacklers.
 Check it out.
 Just another day at the office for @MALACHITONEY2 🤷‍♂️ 📺: ESPN https://t.co/MgPrv4HPfz
— Miami Hurricanes Football (@CanesFootball) October 24, 2026 
 share with Facebook copy link 3:05 pm, October 24, 2026 What we're excited about today
 After a week of upsets and historic shockers, what does college football have for us this week? Here are some things we'll be watching today:
 Hello, No. 1 
 Miami (Fla.) is ranked No. 1 for the first time since the 2002 season. How long can the Hurricanes stay here? The top-ranked team has gone down to unranked teams two weeks in a row — and now Miami plays unranked Pitt. The No. 1 team has never lost to an unranked foe in three consecutive weeks.
 Road tests in the SEC 
 Three top-10 SEC teams fell last week: Georgia, Alabama and Texas. This week also looks dangerous for three of the league's top contenders. No. 7 Ole Miss has to play at No. 19 Texas — a team that was ranked No. 1 only two weeks ago.
 No. 11 Tennessee must go to South Carolina, which is just 1-3 in the SEC but clobbered then-No. 16 Florida in Gainesville 38-19 on Oct. 10. QB LaNorris Sellers threw four TD passes in the win while rushing for another score.
 And what does Auburn have for an encore? After stunning top-ranked Georgia last week, the Tigers come home to take on Lane Kiffin and No. 18 LSU.
 Undefeated watch 
 Only five teams are unbeaten — and three are in the Big 12. We had six going into the week, but James Madison fell to App State Thursday night in OT.
 Here's when the undefeated play today:
 No. 1 Miami: 12 p.m. ET vs. Pitt on ESPN
 No. 2 BYU: 3:30 p.m. vs. UCF on FOX
 No. 8 Texas Tech: 12 p.m. at Cincinnati on FS1
 No. 9 UCLA: 3:30 p.m. vs. Michigan State on CBS
 No. 10 Utah: 10:15 p.m. vs. No. 14 Houston on ESPN
 share with Facebook copy link 2:25 pm, October 24, 2026 ICYMI: Friday's late night drama
 No ranked teams have played this week — yet — but there has already been some drama.
 Last night, Duke, Army and Stanford all picked up dramatic, tight wins.
 Duke wins on trick play 
 Blue Devils RB Nate Sheppard threw a 28-yard TD pass with a little more than 1 minute remaining to lift Duke (5-2 overall, 2-2 ACC) to a 19-16 win at Virginia.
 Sheppard entered the game as the ACC's top rusher, but the Virginia defense held him to only 55 yards on 15 carries. The Cavaliers (4-4, 2-3), however, couldn't get the final stop as they lost for the third time in four games.
 DOUBLE PASS FOR THE LEAD https://t.co/BVNgxUQouk
— Duke Football (@DukeFOOTBALL) October 24, 2026 
 Army tops Tulsa on 50-yard FG 
 Dawson Jones' 50-yard field goal on the last play of the game gave Army a 38-35 win at Tulsa.
 The Black Knights (5-2 overall, 4-1 American) rushed for 275 yards and four touchdowns, led by Godspower Nwawuihe (135 yards, TD) and QB Cale Hellums' 121 yards and three scores.
 Jones had two long kicks on the day, as he kicked a career-long 51 yarder in the first quarter. He also converted on a 34-yard attempt before halftime.
 No doubter from 50 by Dawson Jones FTW 🤩 #GoArmy https://t.co/MOUAiyefWT
— Army Football (@ArmyWP_Football) October 24, 2026 
 Stanford's Warren pilots Cardinal to win 
 Stanford QB Davis Warren had a big night, passing for 303 yards and four touchdowns as the Cardinal beat NC State 31-28.
 The Cardinal (4-4 overall, 2-3 ACC) won again at home, improving to 4-1 on The Farm — the only loss coming to now-No. 1 Miami. However, Stanford is 0-3 on the road, being outscored by more than 44 points per game. Three of the Cardinal's next four games are on the road.
